summary: Static + unit testing of Node.js SAP EBidding bot fixes (global submit mutex + IST scheduler + silent-201 fallback). node --check passes cleanly on bid-engine.js. All 5 unit-test groups in tests/test-window-scheduler.js pass (msUntilNextWindow 7 cases, isHotWindow 22 cases, globalSubmitMutex serialisation 4 concurrent submits, sequential fallback s1->s2->s3->s4 stops at first non-silent-fail, all-silent-fail triggers cooldown). Static code review confirms all 8 claimed changes are present and correct.
critical_code_review_comments: bid-engine.js is 1381 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Consider splitting into modules (mutex.js, scheduler.js, batchHandler.js, sessionManager.js) for maintainability. Not blocking.

Line 1355: Promise.all(...) inside pre-warm branch is unawaited/unassigned (fire-and-forget). The comment says so explicitly, which is fine, but any rejection inside .catch handlers is silently swallowed — consider a debug log on failure to aid future troubleshooting.

Line 963 guard `finalOutcome && finalOutcome.silentFail` combined with `allSilentFail` flag is slightly redundant — allSilentFail alone (initialised true, only set false on real outcome) suffices; harmless but adds a tiny cognitive cost.

TIME_ENDED_COOLDOWN_MS is reused for the all-sessions-silent-fail cooldown; semantically it's a different event (anti-fraud lockout, not window close). Consider a separate env var (e.g. SILENT_FAIL_COOLDOWN_MS) for independent tuning.

verified_changes.sequential_fallback: PRESENT at bid-engine.js:941-960 — iterates ctx.sessions, silent-fail continues to next session, real result breaks.

verified_changes.pre_warm_trigger: PRESENT at bid-engine.js:1351-1356 — 30s threshold, ≤once per 60s window, log message 'Pre-warming for next SAP bid-window' present.
verified_changes.adaptive_sleep: PRESENT at bid-engine.js:1360-1371 — matches spec exactly (0/30/100/500/2000 ms tiers).

verified_changes.runAll_single_worker: CONFIRMED at bid-engine.js:983 — returns [runAll()] (single serialised worker, sessions used as fallbacks).
